When we unquote a type hint, we don't always have to add `from __future__ import annotations`: we don't need it if all the unquoted names are imported. However, `ruff` does add this line whenever it unquotes, even if not necessary. To see this, check the diff at the file `qiskit_ibm_runtime/api/rest/runtime.py`: `from __future__ import annotations` is added although both `ProgramJob` and `RuntimeSession` are imported anyway.

Is there a way to change this PR, to configure ruff, such that it will not add `from __future__ import annotations` in such cases?

Another question: can we enable ruff to automatically add `from typing import TYPE_CHECKING` and `if TYPE_CHECKING:` whenever a name is used only in type hints?
CC @mriedem indeed for review and the above questions.

> Is there a way to change this PR, to configure ruff, such that it will not add `from __future__ import annotations` in such cases?

No, I don't think so. With the previous config, if the import was not present, `UP037` and others were not checked in the file (so quoted type hints were allowed). With this config, if the import is not present, `UP037` is checked in the file, _and_ `ruff` adds the import. I did not find anything in the configuration to tweak further.

Overall, I consider this leaves us in a better situation regarding the codebase (ie. we don't have quoted type hints) and the convention on usage of the import (ie. we just rely on `ruff` choice, and in some edge cases in `pylint` needs - 60625fc). And in the meantime, we can probably count on `ruff` becoming more smarter (maybe https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/18502 hints in that direction) to reduce the number of imports.

> Another question: can we enable ruff to automatically add from typing import TYPE_CHECKING and if TYPE_CHECKING: whenever a name is used only in type hints?

Nice suggestion! I think the `TC` [rules](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/#flake8-type-checking-tc) would probably help, and I would love to be more homogeneous on the usage of `TYPE_CHECKING` (and ideally shave some import time / maybe clean-up some import cycles). I'll spin-off a new issue!

I have a few questions: 

1. Is it correct to say that the order of processing is first broadcast parameter configurations with noise scale, then with `shape`, then the output shape is appended with number of shots and bits - e.g. the output shape is essentially
 (num _randomization, num_param_configs, num_noise_scales, num_shots, creg_size)?
3. How are the shots specified in `QuantumProgram` distributed? E.g. if I have `shots=1024` and `num_randomization=10)`, is it 1024 shots or 1024/10 shots for each randomization ? 
4. Does the `shape` say anything about the execution batching and ordering? For example, if the randomization has a shape of (2, 3), does it imply 2 batches of execution at all? 
5. If I add the twirling annotation but doesn't give a `shape`, does it mean there is only 1 randomization? 
6. The [SLC tutorial](https://qiskit.github.io/qiskit-addon-slc/tutorials/01_getting_started.html) uses `shape=(num_randomizations,)`. But according to this doc, if the Input shape is  `(N,)`, then `shape` should be `(N, num_randomization)`?

@jyu00 

>1. Is it correct to say that the order of processing is first broadcast parameter configurations with noise scale, then with shape, then the output shape is appended with number of shots and bits - e.g. the output shape is essentially
(num _randomization, num_param_configs, num_noise_scales, num_shots, creg_size)?

In the case where you set up a program item such that the extrinsic shape is 3-d with axis interpretations `num _randomization, num_param_configs, num_noise_scales`, then yes, output bit data will be of shape `(num _randomization, num_param_configs, num_noise_scales, num_shots, creg_size)`. However, this is a user choice, they could have set it up as `num_param_configs, num_randomization, num_noise_scales` if they had wanted to.

> 2. How are the shots specified in QuantumProgram distributed? E.g. if I have shots=1024 and num_randomization=10), is it 1024 shots or 1024/10 shots for each randomization ?

The `shots` in the `QuantumProgram` instruction gets applied to every element of every item, and there is no distinction made between randomization axes and other axes. So in your particular example, there will be 10240 shots in total. 

> 3. Does the shape say anything about the execution batching and ordering? For example, if the randomization has a shape of (2, 3), does it imply 2 batches of execution at all?

Ideally, (pseudocode) `chunk(flatten(item), item.chunk_size)` corresponds to batches. However, we don't (and can't) yet promise that. We can chat more on this point.

> 4. If I add the twirling annotation but doesn't give a shape, does it mean there is only 1 randomization?

Correct, when a twirling samplex is present on some item, every element of the item will be randomized, so you effectively get 1 randomization per configuration if you do not add any randomization axes.

> 5. The [SLC tutorial](https://qiskit.github.io/qiskit-addon-slc/tutorials/01_getting_started.html) uses shape=(num_randomizations,). But according to this doc, if the Input shape is (N,), then shape should be (N, num_randomization)?

> Presumably environment options (like job_tags) will go there as well?

The goal is to have feature parity, so we'll start off with all of the things the Executor natively accepts. I tried to highlight the most important options in this category, but you're right to point out that there are other options to consider. I will amend the issue or add a new one.

> Presumably the new SamplerV2 will continue to support local testing mode, given it uses BackendSampler right now which still exists?

That's a good question. Currently the `Executor` doesn't support simulators, so we are limited in our ability to directly work in local mode. Using `BackendSampler` could be a fallback for some of the simpler inputs (no twirling etc.) but I don't think it can provide a general solution here.

Please explain the changes of 6a6abac, and how they are related to Matt's question, [this comment](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/pull/2561#issuecomment-3890303831) is not detailed enough.

The core change is:
```
-    while job.status() not in ["DONE", "CANCELLED", "ERROR"] and time_out > 0:
+    while job.status() not in ["DONE", "CANCELLED", "ERROR", status] and time_out > 0:
```

The `while` would not exit when calling `wait_for_status(job, "QUEUED")`. There was another bug where the comparisons would always fail (passing `JobStatus`, and comparing to `str`). Both of them caused the changed tests to be always skipped or run for longer than expected, instead of the intended behavior. I found the bug while running the `delete_job` test, and felt it would be worth fixing as part of this PR.

So, is this what happened?

- The bug in `wait_for_status` made the executions fail with 401 or 403, and the test was skipped
- So you fixed `wait_for_status`, and only when you fixed it the bugs in `test_retrieve_job.py` showed up (why only then?)

* `test_delete_job` passed prior to 6a6abac
* `test_delete_job_queued` skipped prior to 6a6abc (due to the raise in `wait_for_status`) and seemed it was taking longer than ideal and making more queries to the API than imagined
* no 401 or 403 are involved

So I looked into `wait_for_status`, fixed the logic, and then searched over the codebase for usages of `wait_for_status`, and fixed them (and run the modified tests).
